themes.title: Textiles - apparel/home-textile exports + synthetics
themes.need: India textiles ride three tailwinds at once: China+1 sourcing shifts, the India-UK FTA (signed) + India-EU FTA (advancing), and US tariff normalization - favouring apparel exporters (GOKEX/PGIL/PDSL) and US-heavy home-textile names (WELSPUNLIV/HIMATSEIDE). A second leg = value-added synthetics/recycling (FILATEX, SANATHAN, CENTENKA, GANECOS) and cotton-yarn spread recovery (VTL/NITINSPIN/SPORTKING) plus branded apparel (PAGEIND, ARVIND, RAYMONDLSL).
themes.driver: FTA implementation + US-India trade-deal clarity; festive/wedding demand; cotton-yarn spread; anti-dumping rulings.

hero.oneLiner: The deck positions Karnika as "India's largest Integrated Kidswear Platform at Scale" — an asset-light, outsourced-manufacturing kidswear maker with 15+ years of legacy in integrated manufacturing, brands and distribution, now forward-integrating into consumer retail via the KidCity acquisition.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Claims to be "India's largest Integrated Kidswear Platform at Scale", with an "Asset-Light Model Delivering Superior Capital Efficiency" and "4 Manufacturing Facilities in Howrah (WB) Enabling Scalable Operations".
- Operational metrics cited: 28 states distributed PAN India, 500+ SKUs, 2500+ trusted clients, 90% repeat clientele, 45 lakh production volume (garments) and ISO 14001 certification.
- Omnichannel model spans six routes — distributors (150+), marketplace partnerships, institutional/B2B, D2C (kidcity.shop), kiosks (55+, on airports and high-end streets) and shop-in-shop across Pothy's, Spencer's and Chennai Silks counters.
- Domestic-heavy: "28 States Covered", "150+ Distribution Partners" and "<1% Revenue from Exports (As of Q1FY26)", with export presence described as Middle East and Southeast Asia.
- Market framing: India's children's apparel market USD 11.1 bn (2025) to USD 17.4 bn (2034F) per Statista/Imarc, with the organised share shown as 36% (FY15), 59% (FY25) and 67% (FY30).

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)
capital_allocation.body:
- Deleveraging is a stated priority — "Sharp Reduction in Leverage Levels": Net Debt/Equity 2.8x (FY23), 1.0x (FY24), 0.8x (FY25), 0.8x (FY26).
- SME IPO proceeds were applied to "debt reduction, working capital support, and modernization initiatives" per the 2023 timeline entry.
- Return ratios framed as improving: ROCE 17.5% (FY24), 21.8% (FY25), 25.5% (FY26) and ROE 19.0% (FY24), 25.5% (FY25), 29.0% (FY26).
- Equity actions in 2025: a bonus share issue in the ratio of 1:4, alongside the Kidcity stake acquisition; the deck states no dividend policy.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] Acquired a 75% controlling stake in Kidcity, described as "a fast-growing D2C and omni-channel kidswear brand" (timeline year 2025); a dedicated "Karnika + KidCity Acquisition Rationale" slide cites end-to-end integration, cost advantage, expanded reach, diversified revenue streams and a platform for profitable growth.
- [Corporate action] Bonus share issue in the ratio 1:4 (timeline year 2025).
- [Listing history] Foundation 2008 in Howrah, WB; formalised as Karni International (2017); incorporated as Karnika Industries Limited (2022); automation, ERP and export initiation (2023); SME IPO and NSE Emerge listing (2024, per timeline ordering).
- [Consolidation] FY26 balance sheet shows a Non Controlling Interest of 2 INR Cr, consistent with the 75% Kidcity holding being consolidated.
- [Promoter/board] Board is family-led — Niranjan Mundhra (Chairman & Managing Director), Mahesh Kumar Mundhra and Shiv Shankar Mundhra (Whole-Time Directors), Kirti Mundhra (Non-Executive), with two Independent Directors.
